title: Ethiopian flood basalts
summary: Most of the Ethiopian flood basalts erupted about 30 million years ago, over a period of one million years or less, according to a 1997 Nature study that tied them to the arrival of the Ethiopian-Afar plume head at the Earth's surface. The same study links the eruptions to a shift to colder, drier global climate and an Antarctic ice-sheet advance. A CNR page agrees on around 30 Ma and places plateau uplift at the same time or soon after.

uncertainty.note: The bulk erupted over 1 Myr or less according to Hofmann et al. (1997). Years are Ma counted back from the present.

as_recorded.value: erupted approximately 30 Myr ago, over a period of 1 Myr or less

where.modern_name: Ethiopian Highlands, Ethiopia (proxy pin; the basalts cover the plateau)
where.historical_name: Ethiopian plateau on the African plate near the Afar plume, Oligocene; no polities exist

paleo.note: Highlands proxy at 30 Ma. MULLER2019 gives 5.11 N, 31.59 E and PALEOMAP 6.74 N, 34.52 E.

importance.justification: A large flood-basalt eruption linked in the sources to the Afar plume and to global climate change.
